Hypothesis 1: Individuals with higher levels of perceived social support and parental closeness at Wave 1 will show a significantly flatter rate of increase in depressive symptoms across Waves I–IV, compared to those with lower perceived parental closeness and social support.
Analysis: Latent Growth Curve Analysis 
```{r}
library(lavaan)

#starting with a simple model structure and gradually adding complexity
#Have to use age based loadings instead of by wave because the waves in our data set are unevenely distributed (e.g., w1-w2 = 1 year, w2-w3 = 6 years, w3 to w4 = 6-7 years)

# Compute mean loadings from your data
mean_age_w1 <- mean(combined$age_w1, na.rm = TRUE)
t2_loading <- mean(combined$age_w2, na.rm = TRUE) - mean_age_w1
t3_loading <- mean(combined$age_w3, na.rm = TRUE) - mean_age_w1
t4_loading <- mean(combined$age_w4, na.rm = TRUE) - mean_age_w1
#getting weights of each time depending on mean age and differnece from W1

print(c(t2_loading, t3_loading, t4_loading))

#model with just intercept and slope
model_baseline <- '
  i =~ 1*cesd_w1_mean + 1*cesd_w2_mean + 1*cesd_w3_mean + 1*cesd_w4_mean
  s =~ 0*cesd_w1_mean + 0.592*cesd_w2_mean + 
                        5.788*cesd_w3_mean + 
                        12.968*cesd_w4_mean
'
```

```{r}
fit_baseline <- growth(model_baseline,
                   data    = combined,
                   missing = "FIML")

summary(fit_baseline, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)
#sig intercept: variation in indiviudal depression levels
#sig slope: significant individual differences in trajectories of depression across time
#Intercept-Slope Covariance: 



```
```{r}
#See if protective factors + parental closeness predict difference in trajectories of depression 

model_conditional <- '
  i =~ 1*cesd_w1_mean + 1*cesd_w2_mean + 1*cesd_w3_mean + 1*cesd_w4_mean
  s =~ 0*cesd_w1_mean + 0.592*cesd_w2_mean + 
                        5.788*cesd_w3_mean + 
                        12.968*cesd_w4_mean

  # Protective factors predicting intercept and slope
  i ~ parent_closeness + protective_factors
  s ~ parent_closeness + protective_factors
'

fit_conditional <- growth(model_conditional, data = combined, missing = "FIML")
summary(fit_conditional, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)
#Intercept Paths — Both Significant: Both protective factors significantly predict lower baseline depression at age 15. The effect of perceived social support (protective_factors) is notably stronger (β = -0.396) than parent closeness (β = -0.167). Higher protective factors at wave 1 = lower starting point on the CES-D.


#Slope Paths — Your H1 Test: Both are significant but the direction is positive, which is counterintuitive and needs careful interpretation. This does not mean protective factors worsen trajectories. Remember the mean slope was negative (-0.002) — depression generally decreases over time. A positive coefficient on the slope means protective factors are associated with a less steep decrease, not an increase. This is actually a classic fan-spread interaction with the intercept — people with more protective factors start lower (intercept effect) and therefore have less room to decrease further. The residual intercept-slope covariance (-.285, p < .001) confirms this: people who start higher decrease more steeply.



```


```{r}

model_h1_final <- '
  i =~ 1*cesd_w1_mean + 1*cesd_w2_mean + 1*cesd_w3_mean + 1*cesd_w4_mean
  s =~ 0*cesd_w1_mean + 0.592*cesd_w2_mean + 
                        5.788*cesd_w3_mean + 
                        12.968*cesd_w4_mean

  # Protective factors predicting intercept and slope
  i ~ parent_closeness + protective_factors
  s ~ parent_closeness + protective_factors

  # Covariates
  i ~ BIO_SEX  + PA55
  s ~ BIO_SEX  + PA55
'

#PA55 = parental income at wave 1
#PA12 = parent's education level

fit_model_h1_final <- growth(model_h1_final, data = combined, missing = "FIML")
summary(fit_model_h1_final, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

#Parent closeness and perceived social support both significantly predict lower baseline depression at age 15, with moderate to large effects
#Both protective factors significantly predict the slope even after controlling for sex and PA55 (income w1)
# The positive slope direction -> those with more protective factors start lower and converge toward the sample mean over time, rather than showing steeper declines
#Covariates do not explain away the protective factor effects — the paths remain stable from the conditional to the final model, suggesting robust associations
```

```{r}
#Compare models


anova(fit_baseline, fit_conditional, fit_model_h1_final)
```
```{r}
###Hypothesis 2:  Distinct trajectory subgroups of depressive symptoms across adolescence and adulthood are differentially predicted by early parent relationship quality
#There will be identifiable subgroups following distinct depressive symptom trajectories (e.g. chronically high, adolescent-limited, low-stable) across Waves I–IV, and membership in more adverse trajectory classes will be predicted by lower parental warmth and closeness at Wave I, above and beyond demographic covariates.
#This is your LCGA hypothesis — it integrates the trajectory modelling with your parent relationship variables in a theoretically motivated way. The first part (identifying trajectory classes) maps directly onto developmental psychopathology frameworks like Moffitt's taxonomy, which distinguishes life-course-persistent from adolescence-limited patterns. The second part (predicting class membership) tests attachment and parenting theory: warm, close parent-child relationships in adolescence are theorised to be a key protective factor against persistent psychopathology.
#Analytically this is the two-stage LCGA approach we discussed — lcmm for trajectory identification, then multinomial logistic regression predicting class membership from your H1WP9, H1WP10, H1WP13, H1WP14, H1PF1–H1PF5, H1PF23–H1PF25 parent relationship composites, with demographic covariates (sex, race, parental SES) included as controls. The reference category would be the low-stable trajectory class, and you'd interpret relative risk ratios for each adverse class.


library(lcmm)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

# Reshape combined (wide) into long format for lcmm
lcga_long <- combined %>%
  select(AID, cesd_w1_mean, cesd_w2_mean, cesd_w3_mean, cesd_w4_mean,
         age_w1, age_w2, age_w3, age_w4) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(cesd_w1_mean, cesd_w2_mean, cesd_w3_mean, cesd_w4_mean),
    names_to = "wave", values_to = "cesd"
  ) %>%
  mutate(wave_num = case_when(
    wave == "cesd_w1_mean" ~ 1,
    wave == "cesd_w2_mean" ~ 2,
    wave == "cesd_w3_mean" ~ 3,
    wave == "cesd_w4_mean" ~ 4
  )) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(age = case_when(
    wave_num == 1 ~ age_w1,
    wave_num == 2 ~ age_w2,
    wave_num == 3 ~ age_w3,
    wave_num == 4 ~ age_w4
  )) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(AID, wave_num, age, cesd) %>%
  arrange(AID, wave_num)

# lcmm needs a numeric ID, not a character AID
lcga_long <- lcga_long %>%
  mutate(id_num = as.numeric(factor(AID)))

head(lcga_long, 12)

# Check the spread of ages — informs whether a linear or quadratic age term is needed
summary(lcga_long$age)
```
```{r}
set.seed(123)

m1 <- hlme(
  cesd ~ age,
  subject = "id_num",
  random = ~ age,
  ng = 1,
  data = lcga_long,
  na.action = 1   # listwise deletion within lcmm; FIML-equivalent handling differs from lavaan, flag this
)

summary(m1)
```

```{r}
m2 <- hlme(
  cesd ~ age,
  subject = "id_num",
  random = ~ age,
  ng = 2,
  data = lcga_long,
  mixture = ~ age,
  B = m1
)

m3 <- hlme(
  cesd ~ age,
  subject = "id_num",
  random = ~ age,
  ng = 3,
  data = lcga_long,
  mixture = ~ age,
  B = m1
)

m4 <- hlme(
  cesd ~ age,
  subject = "id_num",
  random = ~ age,
  ng = 4,
  data = lcga_long,
  mixture = ~ age,
  B = m1)

summarytable(m1, m2, m3, m4, which = c("G", "loglik", "conv", "npm", "AIC", "BIC", "%class"))
```

```{r}
library(lcmm)

set.seed(123)

# Re-run m2, m3, m4 with multiple random starting values via gridsearch
# rep = number of random starts to try (50-100 is common in published LCGA work;
# starting smaller here for speed, scale up once you confirm this runs)

m2_grid <- gridsearch(
  hlme(cesd ~ age, subject = "id_num", random = ~ age, ng = 2,
       data = lcga_long, mixture = ~ age),
  rep = 30, maxiter = 10, minit = m1
)

m3_grid <- gridsearch(
  hlme(cesd ~ age, subject = "id_num", random = ~ age, ng = 3,
       data = lcga_long, mixture = ~ age),
  rep = 30, maxiter = 10, minit = m1
)

m4_grid <- gridsearch(
  hlme(cesd ~ age, subject = "id_num", random = ~ age, ng = 4,
       data = lcga_long, mixture = ~ age),
  rep = 30, maxiter = 10, minit = m1
)

summarytable(m1, m2_grid, m3_grid, m4_grid,
             which = c("G", "loglik", "conv", "npm", "AIC", "BIC", "%class"))
```

```{r}
pred <- predictY(m2_grid, lcga_long, var.time = "age")

library(ggplot2)
plot_data <- data.frame(
  age = rep(pred$times$age, ncol(pred$pred)),
  predicted_cesd = as.vector(pred$pred),
  class = factor(rep(1:ncol(pred$pred), each = nrow(pred$times)))
)

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = age, y = predicted_cesd, color = class)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  labs(title = "Predicted depression trajectories — 2-class LCGA solution",
       x = "Age", y = "Predicted CES-D",
       color = "Class")
```

```{r}
# Step 1: fit the 1-class quadratic model first (parallel to m1, but quadratic)
m1_quad <- hlme(
  cesd ~ age + I(age^2),
  subject = "id_num",
  random = ~ age,
  ng = 1,
  data = lcga_long
)

summary(m1_quad)

# Step 2: NOW run the 3-class quadratic gridsearch, initializing from m1_quad
m3_quad_grid <- gridsearch(
  hlme(cesd ~ age + I(age^2), subject = "id_num", random = ~ age, ng = 3,
       data = lcga_long, mixture = ~ age + I(age^2)),
  rep = 30, maxiter = 10, minit = m1_quad
)

summarytable(m1_quad, m2_grid, m3_quad_grid,
             which = c("G", "loglik", "conv", "npm", "AIC", "BIC", "%class"))
```

```{r}
m3_quad_grid <- gridsearch(
  hlme(cesd ~ age + I(age^2), subject = "id_num", random = ~ age, ng = 3,
       data = lcga_long, mixture = ~ age + I(age^2)),
  rep = 30, maxiter = 50, minit = m1_quad   # increased from 10 to 50
)

summarytable(m1_quad, m2_grid, m3_quad_grid,
             which = c("G", "loglik", "conv", "npm", "AIC", "BIC", "%class"))
```
```{r}
pred_quad <- predictY(m3_quad_grid, lcga_long, var.time = "age")

library(ggplot2)
plot_data_quad <- data.frame(
  age = rep(pred_quad$times$age, ncol(pred_quad$pred)),
  predicted_cesd = as.vector(pred_quad$pred),
  class = factor(rep(1:ncol(pred_quad$pred), each = nrow(pred_quad$times)))
)

ggplot(plot_data_quad, aes(x = age, y = predicted_cesd, color = class)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  labs(title = "Predicted depression trajectories — 3-class quadratic LCGA solution",
       x = "Age", y = "Predicted CES-D",
       color = "Class")
```
```{r}
# Check classification quality — postprob() gives average posterior probabilities
# and the proportion of subjects classified with >50%, >70%, >90% confidence
postprob(m3_quad_grid)
```

```{r}
m3_quad_grid_final <- gridsearch(
  hlme(cesd ~ age + I(age^2), subject = "id_num", random = ~ age, ng = 3,
       data = lcga_long, mixture = ~ age + I(age^2)),

)

summarytable(m2_grid, m3_quad_grid, m3_quad_grid_final,
```

```{r}
m3_quad_grid_rep30_maxiter50 <- gridsearch(
  hlme(cesd ~ age + I(age^2), subject = "id_num", random = ~ age, ng = 3,
       data = lcga_long, mixture = ~ age + I(age^2)),

)

summarytable(m3_quad_grid, m3_quad_grid_rep30_maxiter50, m3_quad_grid_rep100,

```
```{r}
# Step 1: just push maxiter up, keep rep modest, see if it even finishes in reasonable time
set.seed(123)

m3_quad_grid_maxiter100 <- gridsearch(
  hlme(cesd ~ age + I(age^2), subject = "id_num", random = ~ age, ng = 3,
       data = lcga_long, mixture = ~ age + I(age^2)),
  rep = 10, maxiter = 100, minit = m1_quad
)

summarytable(m3_quad_grid, m3_quad_grid_rep30_maxiter50, m3_quad_grid_maxiter100,
             which = c("G", "loglik", "conv", "npm", "AIC", "BIC", "%class"))
# Time a single hlme() fit directly, no gridsearch wrapper, to see how long ONE fit takes
system.time({
  test_fit <- hlme(cesd ~ age + I(age^2), subject = "id_num", random = ~ age, ng = 3,
                    data = lcga_long, mixture = ~ age + I(age^2),
                    B = m1_quad, maxiter = 100)
})
```

```{r}
# Use the CONFIRMED stable model (matched maxiter=50, reproducible across rep=30 and rep=100)
# NOT the earlier maxiter=10 result, which we now believe was an under-converged artifact

class_assignments_quad <- m3_quad_grid_rep100$pprob %>%
  select(id_num, class)

id_lookup <- lcga_long %>% select(AID, id_num) %>% distinct()

class_assignments_quad <- class_assignments_quad %>%
  left_join(id_lookup, by = "id_num")

# Merge into combined, dropping any earlier class columns
combined <- combined %>%
  select(-any_of(c("class", "class_label"))) %>%
  left_join(class_assignments_quad %>% select(AID, class), by = "AID")

table(combined$class)
```
```{r}
pred_quad_final <- predictY(m3_quad_grid_rep100, lcga_long, var.time = "age")

library(ggplot2)
plot_data_quad_final <- data.frame(
  age = rep(pred_quad_final$times$age, ncol(pred_quad_final$pred)),
  predicted_cesd = as.vector(pred_quad_final$pred),

)

ggplot(plot_data_quad_final, aes(x = age, y = predicted_cesd, color = class)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  labs(title = "Predicted depression trajectories — confirmed 3-class quadratic LCGA solution",
       x = "Age", y = "Predicted CES-D",
       color = "Class")
```

```{r}
combined <- combined %>%
  mutate(class_label = factor(class,
                                levels = c(1, 2, 3),
                                labels = c("low_stable", "chronic_escalating", "early_elevated_declining")))

table(combined$class_label)

# Confirm low_stable is already the reference (first factor level = reference in multinom)
levels(combined$class_label)
```

```{r}
library(nnet)

multinom_model <- multinom(
  class_label ~ parent_closeness + protective_factors + BIO_SEX + PA55,
  data = combined
)

summary(multinom_model)

# Relative risk ratios (exponentiated coefficients) — easier to interpret than raw logits
exp(coef(multinom_model))

# p-values (multinom doesn't provide these by default)
z_scores <- summary(multinom_model)$coefficients / summary(multinom_model)$standard.errors
p_values <- (1 - pnorm(abs(z_scores), 0, 1)) * 2
p_values
```
```{r}
predicted_class <- predict(multinom_model, type = "class")
table(Predicted = predicted_class, Actual = combined$class_label)

# Overall accuracy
mean(predicted_class == combined$class_label, na.rm = TRUE)
```
